title: Flowise httpSecurity -- T1190 an ipaddr.js kind() mismatch skips every IPv4 deny-list CIDR check for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-69257 (GHSA-c6xh-wv4j-ppv5),
affecting `isDeniedIP()` in Flowise's `httpSecurity.ts` SSRF
protection module.

`isDeniedIP()` compares a resolved IP's `ipaddr.js` `.kind()` against
each deny-list entry's `.kind()` before running the CIDR match. An
IPv4-mapped IPv6 address such as `::ffff:169.254.169.254` reports
`.kind() === 'ipv6'`, while a deny-list entry like `169.254.0.0/16`
reports `.kind() === 'ipv4'` -- the kinds never match, so the CIDR
check is silently skipped entirely for every IPv4 deny rule. The
IPv6-specific deny entries (`::1`, `fc00::/7`, `fe80::/10`) do not
cover the `::ffff:0:0/96` range where these addresses live. An
attacker sets a DNS AAAA record to `::ffff:169.254.169.254` (or any
internal target) and points any of Flowise's 8+ HTTP-emitting
components (HTTP Node, ApiChain, custom-function sandbox, MCP tool,
document loaders) at that hostname -- the deny list, added
specifically to fix the earlier CVE-2026-31829, is completely
ineffective against the mapped form.

Detection logic flags an HTTP-emitting Flowise component resolving a
hostname to an IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal (`::ffff:` prefix) whose
embedded IPv4 address falls in a private, loopback, link-local, or
cloud-metadata range -- the exact bypass shape this advisory's
verified proof of concept (against the actual `ipaddr.js@2.2.0`
Flowise depends on) demonstrates defeats every IPv4 CIDR deny rule.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact function, the `.kind()` mismatch root cause, a
reproducible PoC against the actual dependency version, and a table
of every affected HTTP-emitting code path), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
